govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BurglassCecil_B: Harold Weisberg’s memo on his meeting with Cecil Burglass — on the Ray case — is a researcher’s note. The file belongs to the assassination archive. Weisberg pursued the King case for years. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FerrieDavidWill: This background synopsis of David William Ferrie — from Southern Research Company — is a probe file. Ferrie was a Garrison-probe figure. Its details are disputed. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GouldstonPhil_G: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Jim — surname illegible — on commercial representation is a business note. Weisberg handled his own affairs. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the business archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
isobel-a-romance-of-the-northern-trail: James Oliver Curwood — the beloved storyteller of the Canadian wilderness — weaves a romance of the northern trail. His hero follows duty and love through snowbound forests where danger and beauty walk together. Curwood's passion for the wild gives the love story a magnificent setting.
the-lost-trail: Edward S. Ellis — the dime novelist who created Seth Jones — sends his frontiersmen along the lost trail through Indian country. Ambushes, escapes, and woodcraft fill this fast-moving Western adventure. Classic Ellis: clean, exciting, and full of frontier lore for young readers.
the-boy-aviators-in-africa-or-an-aerial-: John Henry Goldfrap's boy aviators fly to Africa on an aerial ivory trail — hunting adventure from above the savanna. Elephants, dangers, and exotic wonders fill this high-spirited tale. Early aviation meets the dark continent in classic boys'-book style.
the-little-regiment-and-other-episodes-o: Stephen Crane — of Red Badge fame — gathers Civil War episodes of searing intensity in this collection. The title story and its companions show war's confusion, courage, and absurdity with pitiless clarity. Crane's impressionistic genius at full power. No one wrote the chaos and pity of battle more vividly than Crane.
among-malay-pirates-a-tale-of-adventure-: Henty's boys fall among Malay pirates — a tale of adventure and peril in Eastern seas. Daring rescues and jungle fights abound. Exotic excitement in the grand manner. Prahus, krises, and tropical isles provide the thrills. Henty's young heroes outwit the pirates in fine style.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-luxe: The Encyclopedia on Luxeuil, Columbanus' wild Vosges foundation. Irish fire met Frankish woods. Richard Urban Butler tells the tale. Strict rule in a stern land. Eustace carried its rule to new houses across Gaul. The laus perennis never ceased in its choir.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albero-de-mon: A 1913 entry on Albero de Montreuil — the Archbishop of Trier. Henry Brock sketches his strong rule. He rebuilt the church's power on the Moselle. Princes respected his firm hand. A prelate of the reform age. His castle guarded the Moselle crossing.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-rail: This 1913 reference piece on the altar rail — the communion rail of the sanctuary. Augustin Schulte traces its lowly line. Kneeling faithful receive at its gate. Its brass or marble marks the holy. The threshold of the sanctuary. Its gate opens for the bride.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-gaubi: A 1913 entry on Antoine Gaubil — the Jesuit astronomer of Peking. Henri Cordier honors his long mission. His letters taught Europe about China. The emperor prized his science. A missionary of the celestial court. His star maps guided the navigators. His correspondence fills the Jesuit archives.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-margi: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Antonio Margil — the Franciscan apostle of Texas. Zephyrin Engelhardt honors his long missions. He walked from Mexico to Louisiana. The frontier knew his tireless zeal. The friar of the far missions. His missions dotted the Texas rivers.
